title: Merkato traders’ strike/closures over tax and receipt rules
location: Merkato, Addis Ababa; reports mention nearby market areas but no protest venue
scope: Traders closed businesses or operated in shifts while contesting tax increases and receipt requirements. Sources report a strike and government meeting, but not a public street gathering.
organizer: Merkato traders/business owners; named organizer unknown.
threshold_50_evidence: The reported number describes traders on strike, not people assembled simultaneously; threshold and public gathering are unproven.

start_date.summary: APA dates a four-day strike as of 24 Nov; Capital reports closures beginning 18 Nov. Exact start of the collective action remains unclear.

end_date.summary: Sources describe closures in progress and partial business reopening/shifts; end date is unresolved.

location.summary: Market closures in Merkato, Addis Ababa; APA says spread to neighboring market areas.

organizer.summary: Traders/business owners are described as striking; no named organizer is reported.

demands.summary: Protest concerns tax increases and government receipt-based trading requirements.

participants_original.summary: APA calls the strikers hundreds of traders but does not state a simultaneous assembly count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No source identifies a simultaneous public gathering; number of strikers cannot be substituted for event attendance.

protester_violence.summary: No event-specific protester violence claim; unknown.

state_response.summary: City officials met merchants and a fire-damage donation was reported; the report does not establish an event-specific response to a qualifying gathering.

notes: A labor/business action and state tax grievance are documented; the codebook requires a public event, and attendance in such an assembly is not established. No verified candidate.
open_questions: Did traders assemble in a publicly accessible place, or only close shops/work in shifts?
Was any public demonstration/march held, and where and on what date?
Does the “hundreds” estimate refer to simultaneous attendance or total affected businesses?
When did the strike begin and end, and was the dispute primarily a state tax policy demand?

title: Reported multi-site Oromia peace rallies calling on government and armed group to pursue peace
location: Multiple zones in Oromia named as East Shewa, West Shewa, West and Kellem Wollega, Arsi, and Guji; exact towns/woredas unresolved
scope: VOA Amharic describes rallies over two days and competing accounts of organization: some attendees said the government organized them; others said residents called for government and OLA to make peace.
organizer: Organizer and coordination across sites disputed/unknown.
threshold_50_evidence: No simultaneous attendance estimate is reported; counts or scale across zones cannot be aggregated.

start_date.summary: The VOA reports the first rallies on 14 November and a follow-up dated 18 November says they occurred on two days in the prior week; exact first day for every site is not stated.

end_date.summary: Follow-up describes rallies over two days in the prior week; precise site-level end dates are unknown.

location.summary: Six Oromia zones and unspecified woredas are named; town-level locations are not supplied.

organizer.summary: Attendee accounts differ on government organization versus community organization; no single coordinator established.

demands.summary: Some participants said they sought peace from both the regional government and OLA; state response described in follow-up.

participants_original.summary: No crowd estimates reported by site.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Multiple public rallies are reported, but no per-gathering attendance or simultaneous threshold evidence.

protester_violence.summary: No event-specific violence by demonstrators reported; unknown.

state_response.summary: Regional government said it accepted the call for peace; event-specific accommodation/response details beyond public statements are unknown.

notes: Occurrence and some state-directed peace demands are reported, but multi-site event boundaries, ownership and threshold remain unresolved. ACLED cites the VOA coverage, so independence is not assumed.
open_questions: Which individual towns/woredas hosted each gathering, and on which exact dates?
Did any single gathering have at least 50 people simultaneously?
Were these coordinated as one national/regional protest or separate local rallies?
Were the organizers community groups or government offices?
Was the demand directed to Ethiopian government policy, OLA, or both at each site?
Did any rally continue beyond the two reported days or into December?

title: University and town demonstrations after the killing of Dereje Amare
location: Ambo, Jimma, Dire Dawa, Wollega, Arsi, Kotebe Metropolitan, Bule Hora, Haramaya, Asosa, Salale universities; ACLED also names Mizan Tepi, Addis Ababa, Jigjiga, Siltie and Wachemo and unspecified towns
scope: Reports say students and residents demonstrated after a video of a 17-year-old’s killing circulated; The Reporter says demonstrators demanded authorities ensure justice and curb violence. ACLED reports about 26 protests and a police dispersal near Ambo University.
organizer: Students and residents; coordinated organizer unknown.
threshold_50_evidence: About 26 is a count of protests across locations, not a crowd-size estimate; no per-site simultaneous attendance is documented.

start_date.summary: The Reporter article is dated 23 Nov but gives no demonstration dates; ACLED published 26 Nov and describes about 26 protests without exact onset dates.

end_date.summary: No duration or endpoint is reported for individual campus/town demonstrations.

location.summary: At least ten universities are named by The Reporter; ACLED names further campuses and broadly describes towns. Locations cannot be reconciled one-to-one.

organizer.summary: Students and residents participated; no common organizer or nationwide coordination is established.

demands.summary: The Reporter says demonstrators demanded that authorities ensure justice and curb violence.

participants_original.summary: ACLED says around 26 protests occurred but this is the number of events, not people; no participant estimates by site.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No simultaneous crowd size is given for any campus or town.

protester_violence.summary: ACLED describes police dispersal and injuries in Ambo; it does not report protester violence.

state_response.summary: Police forcibly dispersed students near Ambo University and several were injured; the number, response type at other sites and precise timing are unknown.

notes: Two sources document actual demonstrations and a state-directed justice demand, but event-unit boundaries and threshold are not resolved. No event is counted as verified.
open_questions: When did demonstrations begin at each campus/town, and which were in November?
Did at least 50 people attend any single named gathering simultaneously?
Were the campus actions coordinated nationally or independently organized?
Which campuses were included in the estimate of about 26 protests?
What is the exact date and number of injuries in Ambo, and were other state responses reported?
Does any protest episode continue into December?

title: Dera Woreda residents’ public protest demanding rule of law
location: Dera Woreda, North Shewa zone, Oromia; exact site unknown
scope: The Reporter quotes the Oromia Communication Bureau saying residents publicly protested against Fano and OLF-Shene killings/looting and demanded that government ensure rule of law.
threshold_50_evidence: The source does not report crowd size; threshold remains unproven.

start_date.summary: The Bureau statement quoted by The Reporter identifies Friday, 22 November.

end_date.summary: One public protest is described on 22 November; duration/end time is not stated.

location.summary: Dera Woreda, North Shewa zone, Oromia; no town or exact site is supplied.

demands.summary: Residents demanded government ensure rule of law against armed groups.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Occurrence and public nature are reported, but no count or qualitative group-size evidence establishes 50.

protester_violence.summary: No protester violence is described; unknown.

state_response.summary: The Bureau publicized the protest; no other response reported.

notes: Occurrence, date, location at woreda level and domestic government demand are reported via an official Bureau statement; size is unresolved.
open_questions: Did at least 50 people participate simultaneously?
Where in Dera Woreda did the residents assemble?
Was the Bureau statement published contemporaneously and is any independent account available?
Did the protest last beyond 22 November, or connect to separately reported campus demonstrations?
